CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male with type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with complaints of shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient reports swelling in his legs, which he attributes to dietary indiscretion including salty foods at house parties. He describes feeling lethargic. Dyspnea is exertional, occurring with exertion such as walking up stairs. Patient reports one episode of acute dyspnea upon waking approximately one week ago but denies recurrence since then. Patient endorses mild discomfort lying flat and morning stiffness with difficulty ambulating upon waking.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorsed shortness of breath on review of systems sheet. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 1 diabetes mellitus
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Gastroesophageal reflux disease

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump for diabetes management
Omeprazole 20 mg daily for reflux

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient admits to consuming chocolate bars regularly. Alcohol intake noted to be difficult during holiday season but improving. Currently monitoring blood glucose regularly during work week but inconsistent on weekends. Previously performed outdoor stretches for depression management during summer months.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Within normal limits, oxygen saturation adequate at rest
Neck: No jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated
Pulmonary: Crackles appreciated bilaterally at bases
Extremities: 1+ pitting edema noted in lower extremities

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease or pneumonia
Laboratory studies: Normal white blood cell count, no evidence of infection

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute heart failure exacerbation: Start lasix 40 mg daily. Patient instructed to weigh himself daily and report if weight is not decreasing or increasing. Advised to call physician or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest, as may require intravenous diuretics.

2. Type 1 diabetes mellitus: Hemoglobin A1c to be ordered in approximately one month to assess for needed adjustments. Patient to follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam is completed.

3. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications initiated at this time per patient preference.

4. Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily.
